headline: High risk: shared file/network and MCP-capable nullclaw can conflict with cognee’s memory/workspace flows, creating leakage and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee can ingest documents and workflows, while nullclaw can read/write files, run browsers, and use MCP. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content from nullclaw reaches cognee through shared files or MCP-like channels and is treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is not blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF nullclaw writes attacker-controlled content into a workspace cognee reads
IF cognee treats file content as trusted instructions or workflow input
IF the two agents share an MCP or filesystem bridge without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate workspaces so cognee cannot read nullclaw outputs by default
Disable MCP bridges between the agents
Prefix all inter-agent files with a machine-readable provenance header
Require manual review before cognee ingests any nullclaw-generated file
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal and finance data and has network egress, while nullclaw can read/write workspace files and handles API keys, private keys, and bearer tokens. If they share a workspace or account context, sensitive data can flow from cognee into nullclaw outputs or external requests. The blast radius includes secrets and personal data, so this is more than a minor local leak.
conditions: IF cognee and nullclaw share any filesystem or memory namespace
IF nullclaw is allowed to read files containing cognee outputs
IF either agent forwards shared context to a third-party API or webhook
mitigations: Place the agents in separate OS users or containers
Restrict nullclaw to a dedicated workspace directory
Block network egress from any directory containing cognee outputs
Rotate any secrets stored in shared workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, and nullclaw can modify git state, execute shell commands, and use broad network egress. cognee also has session memory and multiple-instance support, so concurrent runs can collide on shared artifacts if they point at the same workspace. The profiles do not show locking or isolation between them, making destructive overwrite or repo-state corruption plausible by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF nullclaw runs shell or git actions while cognee writes artifacts
IF no external lock or lease mechanism serializes writes
mitigations: Assign each agent a distinct repository or workspace
Disable git write access for one agent during shared runs
Use file locks around any shared mutable path
Run only one writer at a time for the shared repo
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and schema structures, and nullclaw can act through shell, browser, webhook, and scheduling tools. That makes it plausible for nullclaw to treat cognee output as authoritative and then execute downstream actions without verification. The pair is not inherently unsafe, but the default tool breadth raises the chance of amplified mistakes.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes cognee output without a verification step
IF cognee emits recommendations that nullclaw converts into actions
IF downstream actions include browser, shell, webhook, or schedule operations
mitigations: Require human approval before nullclaw acts on cognee output
Add a verification step that checks cognee outputs against source data
Limit nullclaw to read-only mode for workflows sourced from cognee
Log and diff every action derived from cognee output
requires-engineering: implement structured provenance and confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while nullclaw handles secrets and workspace files and can send data over broad network egress. The profiles do not state residency, retention, or certification boundaries, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data flows from cognee into nullclaw’s broader operational surface. Uncertainty here should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or finance data is routed from cognee into nullclaw
IF nullclaw stores or transmits that data outside the required residency boundary
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two agents
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Keep regulated data out of nullclaw workspaces
Document retention and deletion rules for both agents
Restrict nullclaw egress for regulated datasets
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
